rationale: The canonical assertion reads gateway-owned host log files and drives a host-local control topology that the nonprivileged Kubernetes client pod cannot access.
re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when the Kubernetes harness provides a canonical gateway log evidence channel and a pod-reachable control endpoint for the duplex fixture.

re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate after a dedicated OpenLDAP sidecar or Service and an external-fixture scenario mode preserve the same protocol and certificate assertions.

rationale: The scenario loads host-local generated CA and expired client fixtures and probes numeric shared TLS listeners unavailable to the Kubernetes client pod.
re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when the Kubernetes harness mounts the same certificate generations and exposes dedicated reachable TLS and mTLS Health Services.

rationale: The scenario injects challenge ownership and expiry through resource status, while ordinary Kubernetes apply cannot write the ACME status subresource used by the Controller.
re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when the Kubernetes runner can patch the ACME status subresource at each phase and expose the dedicated challenge listeners.

re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when the Kubernetes harness deploys the independent processor, its TLS material and admin API, and checks its live observations.
